title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events, say what you did and didn't do, and use the ergative marker ले correctly.
intro:
This is a big unit. You'll learn the **simple past** — म गएँ 'I went', ऊ आयो 'he came' — and the past of 'to be', **थियो** 'was'.

You'll also meet the famous **ergative marker ले**. In the past tense, when the verb has an object (eat *something*, see *someone*), the subject takes -ले: **मैले** भात खाएँ 'I ate rice'. Unlike Hindi, the Nepali verb still agrees with the subject, so ले is easier than it looks. And ले is used more widely too — for tools ('with'), causes ('because of') and to highlight the doer.

vocab.note: मैले, तिमीले, उसले, उनले, उहाँले, तपाईंले, कसले 'who (did)'.
Past of हुनु. के भयो? 'what happened?'; ठीक भयो 'it's fine / it worked out'.
म थिएँ, हामी थियौँ, तिमी थियौ, ऊ थियो (f थिई), उनीहरू थिए, तपाईं हुनुहुन्थ्यो.
Past: भन्यो, भनेँ. Person told takes -लाई.

vocab.en: to go around, travel, sightsee; to turn
vocab.note: घुम्न जानु 'to go on an outing/trip'.

vocab.en: to leave, depart; to be missed/left behind
vocab.note: बस छुट्यो 'the bus left (without me)' = 'I missed the bus'.

vocab.en: to break down, go wrong, spoil

vocab.note: कुरा गर्नु 'to talk, chat'; के कुरा? 'what's the matter?'
Also गिफ्ट / कोसेली (a gift brought back from a trip).
दुई वर्ष अघि 'two years ago'; अघि नै 'already, earlier'.

phrases.en: Last year I went to India.
Have you ever been to Everest?

grammar.title: The simple past
grammar.body:
Simple past endings (consonant stem गर्-):

म **गरेँ** *gareṃ* · हामी **गर्‍यौँ** *garyauṃ*
तँ **गरिस्** *garis* · तिमी **गर्‍यौ** *garyau*
ऊ **गर्‍यो** *garyo* (f **गरी** *gari*) · उनी **गरे** *gare* (f **गरिन्** *garin*) · उनीहरू **गरे**
तपाईं/उहाँ **गर्नुभयो** *garnubhayo*

Vowel stems: खानु → **खाएँ, खायौ, खायो, खाए, खानुभयो**; आउनु → **आएँ, आयो, आए**. Irregular: **जानु → गएँ, गयो, गए**; **हुनु → भएँ, भयो, भए**; दिनु → दिएँ, दियो; लिनु → लिएँ, लियो.

**Negative**: म **गरिनँ** · हामी **गरेनौँ** · तिमी **गरेनौ** · ऊ **गरेन** · उनीहरू **गरेनन्** · तपाईं **गर्नुभएन**.

**'Was'**: छ and हो share one past, **थियो**: म थिएँ, तिमी थियौ, ऊ थियो, उनीहरू थिए, तपाईं **हुनुहुन्थ्यो**. Negative: थिइनँ, थिएन, थिएनन्.

For something further in the past or a past state, Nepalis often use **-एको थियो** ('had done'): म पोहोर भारत गएको थिएँ. And **-एको छ** is the perfect 'have done': म नेपाल धेरै पटक आएको छु 'I've come to Nepal many times'.

examples.en: I went to bed early yesterday.

grammar.title: The ergative ले in the past
grammar.body:
In the simple past (and the perfect -एको छ), the subject of a **transitive** verb — one that takes an object: eat, see, say, buy, do — gets **-ले**:

**मैले** भात खाएँ 'I ate rice' · **उसले** चिठी लेख्यो 'he wrote a letter'

Pronoun + ले: म → **मैले** · हामी → **हामीले** · तँ → **तैँले** · तिमी → **तिमीले** · तपाईं → **तपाईंले** · ऊ → **उसले** · उनी → **उनले** · उहाँ → **उहाँले** · उनीहरू → **उनीहरूले** · यो → **यसले** · को → **कसले** 'who'.

**Key difference from Hindi**: the Nepali verb still agrees with the **subject**, not the object. मैले खाएँ (I-form), उसले खायो (he-form), तपाईंले खानुभयो (polite form) — whatever was eaten.

**Intransitive** verbs (go, come, sleep, sit, laugh, cry, arrive, fall) never take ले: **म** गएँ, **ऊ** हाँस्यो.

Careful: some verbs are transitive in Nepali even if they don't feel like it: **मैले बुझेँ** 'I understood', **मैले काम गरेँ** 'I worked', **मैले फोन गरेँ** 'I phoned'.

examples.en: My sister sent me a present.

examples.native: म बजार गएँ, अनि मैले तरकारी किनेँ।
examples.roman: ma bajār gaeṃ, ani maile tarkāri kineṃ.
examples.en: I went to the market and bought vegetables. (no ले with 'went')

grammar.title: ले beyond the past: tools, causes and doers
grammar.body:
-ले is not just a past-tense marker. It has three other everyday uses:

**1. Instrument — 'with, by means of'**: हात**ले** खानु 'to eat with your hand', कलम**ले** लेख्नु 'to write with a pen', नेपाली**ले** भन्नु 'to say it in Nepali'.

**2. Cause — 'because of'**: पानी**ले** बाटो बिग्रियो 'the road was damaged by the rain', ज्वरो**ले** ऊ आएन 'because of fever he didn't come', भोक**ले** 'from hunger'.

**3. Agent in other tenses**: ले often marks the doer in the present and future too, especially to **emphasise or contrast who** does it, for habitual abilities, and with 'must' (-नुपर्छ) and 'what should I do?' (-ने) sentences: रामले राम्रो गाउँछ 'Ram sings well', यो काम **मैले** गर्छु 'I'll do this job (not you)', **मैले** के गर्ने? 'what should I do?'.

examples.en: Nepalis eat rice with their hands.
Many houses collapsed because of the earthquake.
I'll pay the bill. (emphasis: me, not you)

dialogue.title: A weekend in Nagarkot
dialogue.setting: On Sunday morning at the office, Anita asks Tom about his Saturday trip.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: What did you do on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: I went to Nagarkot with friends.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: Great! How did you get there?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: बसमा गयौँ। तर बाटोमा बस बिग्रियो!
lines.roman: basmā gayauṃ. tara bāṭomā bas bigriyo!
lines.en: We went by bus. But the bus broke down on the way!

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: Oh no! So what did you do?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: हामीले एउटा ट्रक रोक्यौँ, अनि ट्रकमा गयौँ!
lines.roman: hāmile euṭā ṭrak rokyauṃ, ani ṭrakmā gayauṃ!
lines.en: We stopped a truck and went in the truck!

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.en: Haha! Did you see the mountains?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: बिहान सूर्योदय देख्यौँ। मैले धेरै फोटो खिचेँ।
lines.roman: bihāna suryoday dekhyauṃ. maile dherai phoṭo khicheṃ.
lines.en: We saw the sunrise in the morning. I took lots of photos.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: एउटा सानो होटलमा। साहुनीले हामीलाई सित्तैमा दही दिनुभयो।
lines.roman: euṭā sāno hoṭalmā. sāhunile hāmilāi sittaimā dahi dinubhayo.
lines.en: At a little eatery. The owner gave us yoghurt for free.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: कस्तो राम्रो! जे भयो, राम्रै भयो।
lines.roman: kasto rāmro! je bhayo, rāmrai bhayo.
lines.en: How lovely! All's well that ends well.

culture: Every journey in Nepal comes with a story — buses break down, landslides block roads, a **बन्द** (general strike) stops all traffic — and Nepalis tell these stories with humour and a shrug: **जे भयो, राम्रै भयो** 'whatever happened, happened for the best'. Notice that a small roadside restaurant is called a **होटल** even if it has no rooms, and the woman who runs it is the **साहुनी** (the man: साहुजी). Bringing back a little gift (**कोसेली**) — sweets, fruit, a local speciality — from any trip is a warm Nepali custom.
